newsitem.title: USA: Qualcomm, TriQuint in RF chip pact.
newsitem.headline: Qualcomm, TriQuint in RF chip pact.

text.p: Qualcomm Inc said Wednesday it has signed a deal with TriQuint Semiconductor Inc to jointly develop integrated circuits for Qualcomm's new generation of wireless phone handsets.
The company said the joint deal covers the radio frequency (RF) circuits required in its Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) Personal Communications Services (PCS) phones.
One focus of the development is on an "RF receive" electronic component which provides radio performance required to comply with the North American IS-95 CDMA standard, it said.

Don Schrock, vice president and general manager of the ASIC Products group for Qualcomm, said that, "We plan to maximize TriQuint's established low cost, high volume commercial manufacturing capability to satisfy Qualcomm's projected demand for CDMA PCS components."

The components will use Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) semiconductor technology and designed by teams at TriQuint and Qualcomm. They will be manufactured at a new plant TriQuint is building in Hillsboro, Ore.
The component design will be designed to maximize radio the frequencies' properties, such as low noise and low distortion, inherent in TriQuint's proprietary gallium arsenide technology.

The low noise feature is required to improve the communications system's sensitivity to wireless signals, maxmizing call quality while allowing cellular transmitters to be spaced farther apart, improving overall system economics.
"This is a major design win for TriQuint," said Ron Ruebusch, vice president and general manager of the Wireless Communications Division for TriQuint.

TriQuint and QUALCOMM said they will also be investigating a wide range of other RF circuits for various CDMA wireless applications, such as wireless local loop and the Globalstar satellite system, they said.

Wireless local loop refers to the use of wireless phones as an alternative means of providing phone service in local regions where traditional copper wire systems are impractical to use. The systems are gaining acceptance in developing countries where the wired infrastructure may be inadequate.

Globalstar Telecommunications Ltd is a partnership of a dozen international phone service providers and equipment makers, including Qualcomm, which are building a global mobile telephone system based on a network of Low Earth Orbital satellites it plans to launch.
TriQuint gained 1-3/8 Wednesday morning to 22-1/2. Qualcomm stock was off one at 41-1/2.
